WHAT WAS CHECKED (7 items), each against a dump I actually read:

Dump used: docs/asmdumps/f2_3B0650.asm (rva 0x3B0650, 512 bytes), which covers FOUR of the five cited siblings byte-for-byte identically: 0x3B0650, 0x3B06A0, 0x3B06F0, 0x3B0740. Its "COMPARE / JUMP PAIRS" section is EMPTY — no float compares in the range, consistent with the C.

1. Role gate. 3B0656 `test edx,edx` / 3B0658 `jne 0x3B069A (ret)`. Recall role (flag=1) is a bare no-op; only host role (edx=0) does work. juno_mod.c models the host role only and has no role argument — consistent with juno_mod.h and docs/P112_FINDINGS.md §3 ("the port drives flag = 1"). Not a defect.
2. off==0 early-out. 3B0661 `test eax,eax` / 3B0663 `je 0x3B068B` — skips the blend and passes the raw base. C line 26 `if (off == 0) return base;`. INTEGER test, exact match.
3. Span selection sign test. 3B0665 `jle 0x3B0671` -> ecx = base (r8d); fallthrough (off > 0) -> 3B0667 `mov ecx,0xff` / `sub ecx,r8d` = 255-base. C line 28 `(off > 0) ? (255L - base) : base`. Exact match; off<0 and off==0 both land on the `base` arm in the plugin, and off==0 is already returned earlier in both.
4. Product. 3B0674 `imul ecx, eax` — 32-bit. C line 29 uses long (64-bit). Bounded |off|<=100, span<=255 => |prod| <= 25500, so no divergence anywhere in the valid domain. Not a defect.
5. Division by 100 and its rounding. 3B0677-3B0686: `mov eax,0x51eb851f ; imul ecx ; sar edx,5 ; mov eax,edx ; shr eax,0x1f ; add edx,eax`. The final `shr/add` of the sign bit is precisely the TRUNCATE-TOWARD-ZERO correction, so the plugin's magic-number divide equals C's `prod / 100L` for BOTH signs. C's comment at lines 30-32 is correct. (This is candidate 5 of docs/CONTROL_AUDIT_CANDIDATES.md — "rate rounding vs truncation", REFUTED 3 of 3 — refuted again here on its own dump.)
6. Accumulate. 3B0688 `add r8d, edx` then the tail-jmp with the result. C line 32 `base + (int)(prod/100L)`. Match.
7. STORE SET (the juno_ramp_reset class of defect). In all four blend siblings the ONLY writes are to registers; each ends `mov rax,[r9] ; xor edx,edx ; mov rcx,r9 ; jmp qword ptr [rax+0x868/0x828/0x8f0/0x8d0]` — a TAIL-CALL to the base parameter's own setter with the computed byte, and NO store to the object. juno_mod_byte is a pure function returning that byte, so there is no missing store and no extra store. The MODS table is data only.

TABLE CROSS-CHECK: MODS[] 312->779, 313->782, 314->781, 315->758, 316->798, 317->794 matches docs/P112_FINDINGS.md §4 row for row. The base-cache offsets read by the dumps corroborate it: 0x4fc=proc[319] (VCF RESONANCE), 0x4dc=proc[311] (DCO PWM DEPTH), 0x540=proc[336] (PORTAMENTO), 0x530=proc[332] (EFFECT DEPTH).

ONE THING I COULD NOT RESOLVE, STATED HONESTLY (not a candidate):
The fifth cited sibling, 0x3B9990, is dumped (docs/asmdumps/f2_3B9990.asm) and does NOT have the blend shape. It tests edx, then `mov edx,[rcx+0x4f8]` (= proc[318], an offset NOT in the P112 base-cache table), calls 0x3B1800, and tail-calls vtable+0x860 — it never reads its own r8d value argument. AT-RISK SITES I COULD NOT ADJUDICATE (list them so a later pass with the right dump can): juno_triangle phase<=1.0f, phase<-1.0f, phase>=-0.5f, phase<=0.5f; juno_wrap_unit x>1.0f and x<-1.0f; juno_wrap_hi x>1.0f. ZERO CANDIDATES. src/juno_hostparams.c cannot host the playbook-81 defect class.

1. COMPLETE COMPARISON INVENTORY (all 151 lines read). Every comparison in the file is INTEGER: the six accessor bounds guards `i>=0 && i<JUNO_HOSTPARAM_COUNT` (lines 112-118, and again at 126/139 through the accessors), the decode sign test `juno_host_param_min(i) < 0 && v >= 128` (line 130), the decode type test `== 0` (line 128), the encode clamp pair `v < min` / `v > max` (lines 141-142), the encode type test `== 0` (line 144), and the two's-complement test `v < 0` (line 143). There is NO float in the file at all -- no float literal, no float variable, no float member in the `juno_hostparam` struct (all fields are `const char*` or `int`), no fabsf/fminf/fmaxf. Therefore checked=0 float comparisons is not an omission: there is nothing of that class to check. x86 unordered semantics (ja/jae/jne/je on ucomiss/comiss) are irrelevant to integer `cmp`/`test`, which have no unordered state.

2. NO CITABLE RVA EXISTS FOR THIS FILE, AND I DID NOT INVENT ONE. Per the discipline rule I state this plainly. The file carries ZERO rva comments -- I grepped it and read it in full. Its own header says it is GENERATED from `truth/Script.xml` value-tree leaves plus the cumulative record-offset map (`scratchpad/gen_host_params_spec.py` -> `host_params_spec.json` -> `scratchpad/gen_hostparams_c.py`). It is a DATA TABLE plus two serialization helpers for the in-browser panel, not a transcription of any plugin subroutine. Consequently there is no plugin function whose STORE SET this file's stores could be compared against, and none of the 24 dumps in docs/asmdumps/INDEX.txt covers it (the index holds cand1-cand6 bend/mod/note/ctor/setsr/ratelaw plus the f2_* and effect_dispatch/setsr_container set -- all render- or control-path DSP, none a Script.xml leaf-table emitter). The store-set half of the task is therefore NOT APPLICABLE here rather than clean-by-inspection, and I report it as such instead of manufacturing a comparison.

3. STORE AUDIT, AS FAR AS IT IS MEANINGFUL. `juno_host_param_encode` is the only function in the file that writes memory. Its write set is exactly: for type 0, one byte `rec[r]`; for type 1/2, the two low nibbles of `rec[r]` and `rec[r+1]`, preserving both high nibbles (`(rec[r] & 0xF0) | ...`). That matches the read law used everywhere else in the port -- `nib()` at src/finefx_recall.c:42 and the ~20 inline `((blob[2*p]&0xF)<<4)|(blob[2*p+1]&0xF)` sites in src/juno_apply.c (lines 472, 520, 622, 696, 722-726, 759-760, 804, 946, 960-962, 977-979). Step trigger f2_3C0260.asm:30 `3C02CC cmp byte ptr [rbx+0xbee], r8b` / `3C02D3 jle 0x1803c04d1` uses it as the slot-loop bound; the ported selectors read the SAME byte as their nslots term: 3BEFCA (sel_up), 3BE5CF (up&down), 3BE6E0 (down), 3BE85F (down-oct). So the port's split into pat_nslots (bound, carp.c:598) and nslots (selector term) is a real cell split, and carp.c:596 writes count into the selector-facing half, making `count - nslots` = 0 instead of `count - pat_nslots`.
- No dump in docs/asmdumps/ contains ANY write to 0xbee (grep: only the 9 reads listed). "Writer absent" is therefore only "absent from the dumped functions" — the pattern-load writer is not covered by any dump. The claim's rva "0x3C02CC (writer absent)" overstates what the evidence supports.

WHY IT CANNOT DIFFER:
1. In all four ported selectors, the only consumer of `count - nslots` is the clamp `if (field56 > v7) field56 = 0` (carp.c:115, 135, 159, 191). field56 has NO other reader in src/carp.c.
2. field56 (a1+0x38) is only ever 0 in the port: the plugin increments it at f2_3C0260.asm:18 `3C0290 inc dword ptr [rbx+0x38]` on the pattern wrap, and the port's step trigger (carp.c:593-596) performs no such increment; carp_init sets it 0 (carp.c:394). With field56 == 0 the clamp is `0 > v7`, false for any v7 >= 0, and when v7 is negative (sel_up does not take max) it assigns 0 to a field already 0. Either way no state changes and no note changes.
So even after fixing this candidate, the emitted event stream is bit-identical. The masking is double: field56 is dead in the port, and it is clamp-only in the four reached selectors. (The unported selectors at 0x3BE790 and 0x3BF0C0 DO use field56 as an index offset — 3BE7D4/3BF0E6 — but they are not reached by TYPE 0..5 and are not transcribed.)

GATE COVERAGE: no gate in tools/verify or tools/engineb mentions nslots (only tools/engineb/d3_voiceindex_gate.c matches the string, unrelated). Nothing covers it — and nothing needs to, since the difference is unobservable at the port's outputs.

NOTE: the true underlying issue is the missing field56 increment (the separate candidate); this store is only its shadow. Fixing 596 alone changes nothing; fixing the increment alone would make 596 matter.
